name: Soft Goods
why: Heavyweight tees, sweatshirts and thermals cut and sewn in its own Detroit factory, open since 2017 and selling under its own name since 2025.
origin: Founded in 2017 in Detroit by Josh York.

cities: No store of its own in the US · its own site, and independent shops

craft_evidence.owned: Operates its own cut-and-sew factory in Detroit: 1927 Rosa Parks Blvd Suite 170, Corktown (Factory page, factory photos, no tour); earlier address 1314 Holden St B-2 (CFDA directory); 6,000 sq ft and about 12 staff (American Manufacturing, 20 Aug 2026). Building ownership vs lease NOT stated anywhere; no filing found. Knitting (North Carolina) and dyeing (South Carolina per Factory page) are outsourced.
craft_evidence.makers: Found Surface (Cleveland) knits the Cotton Cuff Beanie (an accessory); reverse satin labels made in Los Angeles (unnamed). No sewing-factory or dyehouse named; dyer unnamed.
craft_evidence.mills: NONE: regions only (cotton grown in Texas/American South; yarn knit in North Carolina; fleece milled in North Carolina). No mill named on any page read.
craft_evidence.madein: Detroit/USA stated on all Soft Goods-branded clothing pages whose text was read (tees, longsleeve, hoodie, crewnecks, thermal, double-front and jersey pants, raglan, robe, sweatshorts); not seen in text read for Jersey Short and French Terry Sweatpant(s); LEON collab page has no info. Roughly 12 of 14 confirmed.
craft_evidence.heritage: Dated and placed: 2017, second-story warehouse in Corktown, Detroit, three used Juki machines and a cutting table (our-story). Independent: CFDA directory lists founded 2017; American Manufacturing 20 Aug 2026 says Founded in 2017. Own label only since 2025; private-label before.
craft_evidence.process: Partly: spec-level (flatlock construction, 20s/10s singles yarn, 190/305/360 GSM, crossgrain body, garment dyed/washed and pre-shrunk, custom-developed 10.5oz fleece, founder hand-cut and sewed a tee a day to perfect it). No published account of the dyeing step; sources conflict on where it happens.
craft_evidence.reasoning: The brand and the sewing factory are the same operation: a Detroit cut-and-sew floor, dated to 2017, with independent press (AAM 2026, CFDA directory, MEDC 2023) confirming it. It stops short of 5 because knitting and dyeing are done by unnamed outside partners, no mill is named, and building ownership is unproven. Not 3: the making is its own, not just named.

ownership.owner: Josh York, its founder; no outside funding.

opview: “By starting a garment factory, I would not only get to do something I loved, making great clothes, but I could create real jobs and real opportunities for Detroiters” — Josh York, founder, Soft Goods, our story
